text:
Alex: Heads up — after the q4_0 bring-up for llama3-7b yesterday we're seeing two problems in production: (1) a p99 latency regression ~220ms -> ~420ms for chat endpoint, (2) sporadic JSON output truncation / repeated keys in structured responses.
Priya: Ugh. Is this only on the canary pool or across dedicated?
Alex: Canary and a small portion of Dedicated. Canary traffic 12:00–14:00 shows the highest error rate.
Jamie: Saw evaluation diffs too — our schema-accuracy metric for the qa prompt set dropped from 98.5% -> 92.1% after quantize pass. Not consistent across seeds though.
Max: Any repro steps? logs?
Alex: Repro is easy with the sample prompt in #evals: send the JSON schema generator prompt -> sometimes returns duplicate keys like {"answer":..., "answer":...}. Attached log snippet: ```ERROR [2025-10-22T12:15:03Z] model=llama3-7b-q4 task=chat id=usr-9a3 status=ok tokens=312 note="kv-cache-reset?" stack=none```
Priya: Could be a KV-cache eviction edge-case when quantization changes token alignment. Did the runtime change kernel for rotary offsets?
Jamie: We switched to the faster matmul kernel in the q4 path last deploy. I can run a small ablation: q4+old-kernel vs q4+new-kernel.
Max: Meanwhile, we should revert canary to previous model variant (llama3-7b-fp16) for traffic > 95th percentile SLO breaches. /cc @Eva for rollout.
Eva: On it. Starting rollback canary -> baseline now. CI-Bot reports canary deploy id=canary-20251022-172 has health issues flagged.
CI-Bot: [deploy-bot] canary-20251022-172: failing health checks (5% failed request) — auto-rollback scheduled in 5m if not fixed.
Alex: Also seeing tokenization mismatches in a handful of samples that hit non-BPE chars. Repro snippet: ```python
prompt = "Translate to JSON:\n- Title: \"Foo\"\n- Date: 2025-10-22"
resp = client.chat.generate(prompt)
# sometimes resp has duplicated keys
```
Priya: For triage I'm going to: 1) run evals against the canary with deterministic seeds, 2) capture full KV cache traces for failing cases, 3) compare logits between fp16 and q4 runs. Anyone want to take 2?
Jamie: I'll grab the logits diff and deterministic eval. Give me a seed list.
Max: I'll smoke-test the kernel revert on a small GPU pool and run latency microbenchmarks.
Eva: Rollback in progress — canary traffic dropping now. I'll keep you posted.
Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-2025-5423 "llama3-7b-q4 post-launch: p99 latency regression + output schema corruption" severity=high assignee=oncall
Alex: TL;DR checklist for follow-up (so we have a concrete bring-up checklist for future models): - run end-to-end deterministic evals + schema checks before canary, - run tokenization edge-case sweep, - kernel/quantization A/B microbenchmarks (latency + logits diffs), - KV cache eviction stress test, - provenance markers in responses so we can detect modified decoding paths.
Priya: Agreed. I'll add to the onboarding intake form and the runbook.
Jamie: If rollback restores baseline metrics I can still run a postmortem eval to find a minimal repro.
Max: FYI I noticed higher memory fragmentation in the q4 allocator which might explain p99. I'll profile heap during stress.
Eva: Rollback finished. Canary back to baseline (llama3-7b-fp16). Metrics returning to expected ranges.
Alex: Great — assign owners: Jamie (eval diffs & repro), Max (kernel/memory profiling), Priya (onboarding checklist updates), Eva (rollout ops). I'll start a short postmortem doc after we have the diffs.
Priya: Thanks. Please paste any failing prompts into the postmortem doc.
Jamie: will do. saving failing-case list to /evals/postlaunch/llama3-q4-failures-20251022.txt
Max: If anyone needs me I'll be on the infra sprint channel. :wrench:
Eva: Leaving a note in #eng-releases: avoid switching quant kernel and allocator together during first canary.
Alex: Good call. We'll also add a gating evaluation that checks for schema-preserving output.
Priya: Closing loop: update the intake checklist -> add a mandatory "schema-output test" and "kv-cache stress" checkbox before canary.
Alex: Thanks all :thumbsup:
